angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 730,485 km at 8.70 pc = 1.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 114.9497 +/- 0.5280 mas (same row, RUWE 5.62): 8.70 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 1.05 solar radii from Takeda et al. (2007), ApJS 168, 297, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729): 730,485 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.000 (0.960 to 1.040) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5882 K from Valenti & Fischer (2005), ApJS 159, 141, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). Spin inclination 65 degrees and rotation period 5.022 d from Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2, the values of the ZDI inversion (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Valenti & Fischer (2005), ApJS 159, 141, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/chi1-orionis.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.396, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 39587) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
